thread:
jamie: Noticing a pretty wide p99 spike on intra-service calls, lots of 504/502s. Most traces show DNS lookups timing out, not actual downstream timeouts.

sara: Oh interesting — region or cluster-wide?

jamie: Cluster-wide in us-west-2. Affected pods across multiple node pools. CPU/mem fine. Networking graphs show east-west packet loss bump.

anil: Can you paste a sample log?

jamie: Here — from svc-a talking to svc-b:```
2026-03-18T18:12:11.234Z ERROR fetch failed: dial udp 10.96.0.10:53: i/o timeout
2026-03-18T18:12:11.235Z WARN retrying request (1/3)
2026-03-18T18:12:11.987Z ERROR upstream responded 502
```

marta: That ip 10.96.0.10 is cluster DNS (CoreDNS). Any node-local caches?

jamie: We run node-local-dns as daemonset in all pools. Pod logs show node-local resolving but then forwarding to CoreDNS and timing out intermittently.

anil: Could be MTU/fragmentation on the overlay or RDMA interrupts. Any recent kernel or CNI changes?

jamie: No config rolls in the last 24h. We did bump jumbo MTU to 9000 on one of the metal racks last week (for GPU traffic), might be leaking to other overlays via misconfigured routes.

sara: Ops, can we repro directionally? Start a busyloop resolver from a pod and tcpdump on node-local and CoreDNS to see where the UDP drops happen.

jamie: Running quick probe now:```
# from pod
for i in {1..200}; do nslookup svc-b.svc.cluster.local || echo "fail $i"; done
```

deploy-bot: probe job started: job/diagnostic-dns-probe-1815001234 (pods: 5) :rocket:

marta: While that runs, check conntrack counters and NIC rx/tx errors on nodes hosting CoreDNS and node-local. Fragmentation stats too.

anil: Also capture `ip -s link` on nodes and verify `net.ipv4.ip_forward` and `rp_filter` are consistent. If MTU mismatch, we'll see TX drops at layer 2.

jamie: Probe output (summary): 200 lookups -> 36 fails, spikes align with periods of increased GPU training traffic. Node-local logs: `forwarding to 10.96.0.10` then `read udp ... i/o timeout`. CoreDNS logs don't show receive entries for some of the failed queries.

sara: That pattern screams packet loss between node-local and CoreDNS — either network path or oversubscribed kernel NIC queues. Could be RDMA/GPU traffic preempting normal traffic if QoS not isolated.

marta: If CoreDNS isn't receiving the UDP packet, node-local will retry and amplify retries -> fanout and cascaded timeouts. Suggest increasing node-local cache TTL short-term and enabling fallback to 8.8.8.8 for non-critical lookups while we investigate.

anil: Longer term: pin CoreDNS onto nodes with isolated NICs or use multi-replica placement across racks and enable UDP GRO/GSUM tuning. Also consider switching node-local to TCP for forwarding to CoreDNS to avoid UDP frag issues.

jamie: Quick mitigation applied: bumped node-local cache ttl from 5s -> 15s, enabled fallback list [10.96.0.10, 8.8.8.8], and tainted gpu-isolated nodes so CoreDNS pods won't land there. Rolling now.

sara: Good. Can you also capture `ss -uap` during next spike and paste? Need to see retransmits.

jamie: Will do. If mitigation holds, we'll open a postmortem and investigate MTU bleed and RDMA config.

marta: Assigning follow-ups: anil - kernel/CNI MTU audit, jamie - collect ss/tcpdump traces, sara - monitor error budget and rollback plan.

anil: noted. One more ask — correlate GPU network bursts to the failure windows. If QoS shaping absent, GPU egress could monopolize NIC.

jamie: Copy. I'll attach pcap and conntrack dumps to the incident ticket once done. :white_check_mark:
